_provenance.notes: The American Fisheries Act (AFA) of 1998 was landmark federal legislation that rationalized the $1+ billion Bering Sea pollock fishery — the world's largest single-species fishery. Before AFA, the derby fishery had 200+ vessels racing to catch as many fish as possible. AFA created sector allocations and cooperatives, reducing the active fleet from 200+ vessels to approximately 20 vessels. The AFA cooperatives — Pollock Conservation Cooperative (PCC) and others — achieved massive efficiency gains. The AFA also established the CDQ program's pollock allocation. American Seafoods, Trident Seafoods, and 3 other companies control most of the pollock quota.
